headline: High: oh-my-openagent’s broad networked, multi-tool defaults can amplify botpress outputs into unsafe actions and data exposure; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via shared MCP/file channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: botpress has no documented shared channel, but oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and can read files and browser content, so attacker-controlled content from botpress could be treated as instructions if bridged. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF botpress output is copied into an MCP tool, hook, browser, or file that oh-my-openagent parses as instructions
IF the orchestrator exposes a shared workspace or message queue between the two agents
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of botpress outputs into agent B prompts
Add a provenance tag to all botpress-generated text before handoff
Restrict B’s MCP hooks to allowlisted commands only
Review any shared clipboard or file bridge before enabling it
requires-engineering: add instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: botpress is documented with network egress none, while oh-my-openagent has broad egress and touches session history, project code, and provider auth data. If they share a workspace or credentials, B can leak data that A cannot exfiltrate itself; the interaction is plausible in default-style deployments but not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory or credential store
IF B is allowed to upload session history, code, or auth prompts to external providers
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared directory before running B
Disable B features that send code or history to third parties
Rotate any provider credentials exposed to B
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem and credential isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: botpress can install packages, and oh-my-openagent can spawn subprocesses, run browsers, and write to multiple config/file locations. That creates overlapping mutation risk on shared installs or repos; no locking is documented, so concurrent writes could conflict even though the exact shared target is not proven.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository, config directory, or package environment
IF B runs multiple instances while A modifies the same files or dependencies
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate checkout
Freeze package installs during B sessions
Avoid concurrent runs against the same config files
Back up mutable files before starting
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared write paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent exposes team_send_message and task creation APIs, so if it consumes botpress output as authoritative, it can turn a mistaken or injected response into downstream actions. botpress is a customer-support agent, making this a realistic handoff path; the blast radius includes irreversible external messages.
conditions: IF botpress output is forwarded into B without verification
IF B is permitted to send messages or create tasks based on that output
mitigations: Require human review before B sends messages
Add a verification step for botpress-generated facts
Disable team_send_message until outputs are checked
Log and diff all botpress-to-B handoffs
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: botpress is open-source with no residency or retention details here, while oh-my-openagent explicitly handles provider auth prompts, session history, and telemetry and sends data to external services. Because compliance controls are undocumented for both, the safest reading is a mismatch risk on sensitive support data rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated or customer-support data is entered into B
IF B’s telemetry or provider calls are not covered by the operator’s DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B sessions
Review telemetry and retention settings before use
Disable nonessential external API calls
Document which data classes each agent may process
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
